title: ParsCN: A Persian Dataset for Counter-Narrative Generation to Combat Online Hate Speech

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating language models' ability to generate effective, culturally relevant, and non-toxic counter-narratives against hate speech targeting religious groups (e.g., Islam, Judaism) using automated metrics and human evaluations.

Assessing the generation of counter-narratives against hate speech targeting ethnic and racial groups (e.g., Azeris, Kurds, Black Africans) through human scoring (relevance, tone) and automated metrics like BERTScore and Toxicity.

Measuring the quality and cultural appropriateness of model-generated counter-narratives responding to misogynistic and gender-based hate speech using both human evaluations and automated semantic/toxicity metrics.

Evaluating the relevance, effectiveness, and tone of counter-narratives generated by language models in response to hate speech targeting political entities, politicians, or country laws in the Persian context.
Analyzing the performance of language models in generating constructive and non-escalatory counter-narratives against hate speech directed at specific professions (e.g., police, teachers).

Testing language models on their capacity to produce culturally appropriate and non-toxic counter-narratives against xenophobic hate speech targeting specific nationalities and immigrant groups (e.g., Afghans, Chinese, Arabs).
